---
title: "Module Structure"
---

## Layout

```
<project-root>/
├── carrier.toml
├── README.md
└── <src-dir>/
    ├── __init__.R
    ├── mod.R
    ├── mod2.R
    └── <submod>/
        ├── __init__.R
        └── example.R
```

Anyone who knows the shape of a Python package will recognize this: `<project-root>` plays the role of the package's top-level directory, `carrier.toml` plays `pyproject.toml`, and `__init__.R` plays `__init__.py`.

## How the source directory is resolved

`carrier bundle` and `carrier install <dir>` both resolve the source directory the same way, in this order:

1. When `src` is set in `carrier.toml`, that path is used, resolved relative to the project root. It can be just an R script. Otherwise, it must exist as a directory and must contain `__init__.R`. Any directory name is allowed here.
2. By default, when `src` is unset, the source directory must be named *exactly* after `module.name`. There is no fallback search; a mismatch fails the build with an explicit error naming both the expected directory and the module name.

Either way, a missing `__init__.R` at the resolved directory's root fails immediately, with a message pointing at `__init__.R`'s role as the module's entry point.

## `__init__.R`

This is the only file `carrier` treats specially. Everything else under the source directory is bundled as-is. The `carrier bundle` command walks the whole tree and includes every file it finds, so keep build artifacts and scratch files out of the source directory (or point `src` at a directory that doesn't contain them).
